{{short description|Relates the homology of a fiber bundle with the homologies of its base and fiber}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Leray–Hirsch theorem'''<ref>{{citation|first=Allen| last=Hatcher|authorlink=Allen Hatcher| title=Algebraic Topology|publisher= [[Cambridge University Press]] |location=Cambridge |year=2002| url= https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf|isbn=0-521-79160-X}}</ref> is a basic result on the [[algebraic topology]] of [[fiber bundle]]s. It is named after [[Jean Leray]] and [[Guy Hirsch]], who independently proved it in the late 1940s. It can be thought of as a mild generalization of the [[Künneth formula]], which computes the cohomology of a product space as a tensor product of the cohomologies of the direct factors. It is a very special case of the [[Leray spectral sequence]].

==Statement==

===Setup===
Let <math>\pi\colon E\longrightarrow B</math>
be a [[fibre bundle]] with fibre <math>F</math>. Assume that for each degree <math>p</math>, the [[singular cohomology]] rational [[vector space]]
:<math>H^p(F) = H^p(F; \mathbb{Q})</math>
is finite-dimensional, and that the inclusion 
:<math>\iota\colon F \longrightarrow E</math>
induces a ''surjection'' in rational cohomology 
:<math>\iota^* \colon H^*(E) \longrightarrow H^*(F)</math>.
Consider a ''section'' of this surjection 
:<math> s\colon H^*(F) \longrightarrow H^*(E)</math>, 
by definition, this map satisfies 
:<math>\iota^* \circ s = \mathrm {Id}</math>.

===The Leray–Hirsch isomorphism===
The Leray–Hirsch theorem states that the linear map 
:<math>\begin{array}{ccc}
H^* (F)\otimes H^*(B) & \longrightarrow & H^* (E) \\
\alpha \otimes \beta & \longmapsto & s (\alpha)\smallsmile \pi^*(\beta) 
\end{array}</math>
is an isomorphism of <math>H^*(B)</math>-modules.

===Statement in coordinates===
In other words, if for every <math>p</math>, there exist classes

:<math>c_{1,p},\ldots,c_{m_p,p} \in H^p(E)</math>

that restrict, on each fiber <math>F</math>, to a basis of the cohomology in degree <math>p</math>, the map given below is then an [[isomorphism]] of <math>H^*(B)</math> [[Module (mathematics)|module]]s.

:<math>\begin{array}{ccc}
H^*(F)\otimes H^*(B) & \longrightarrow & H^*(E) \\
\sum_{i,j,k}a_{i,j,k}\iota^*(c_{i,j})\otimes b_k & \longmapsto & \sum_{i,j,k}a_{i,j,k}c_{i,j}\wedge\pi^*(b_k)
\end{array}</math>
where <math>\{b_k\}</math> is a basis for <math>H^*(B)</math> and thus, induces a basis <math>\{\iota^*(c_{i,j})\otimes b_k\}</math> for <math>H^*(F)\otimes H^*(B).</math>
